title: Vincent Ferrer (5 April)
hookLine: a Dominican preacher who walked from town to town calling people to repentance
tomorrow: John Baptist de La Salle (7 April)

lines: A CROWD COMING OVER THE HILL.
THE CHURCH WON'T HOLD THEM ALL.
cards: Dust on a road, and a crowd coming over the hill. At the front, an old friar in a black and white habit, walking, or on a donkey when his legs give out.
Behind him, people who left their villages to follow him to the next one: some singing, some weeping, some who came to watch and stayed.
In the town, someone builds him a platform in the square, because the church won't hold them all. He preaches for hours. Then the crowd moves on, and he moves with it.
His name was Vincent Ferrer, and the road was his pulpit.

teach.h: A SCHOLAR IN A SPLIT CHURCH.
teach.b: Vincent was a Dominican from Valencia, in Spain, a scholar and a teacher, and for a while a man of the papal court. His world was split.
The Church had rival popes, each with his own cardinals and followers, and Vincent stood loyally by one of them.

teach.h: SENT OUT TO PREACH ON THE ROAD.
teach.b: Then, the story goes, he fell gravely ill and in a vision was sent out to preach.
He left the court for the road, and spent the rest of his life walking across Spain, France, Italy and beyond, calling people to repentance, to turn back to God before judgment comes.

Tradition tells that people who didn't share his language understood him anyway. Saint Paul, quoting the prophet Isaiah, writes in the Douay-Rheims: "How beautiful are the feet of them that preach the gospel of peace."

teach.h: HE GAVE UP HIS POPE TO HEAL THE SPLIT.
teach.b: His later choice was costly: he withdrew his support from the pope he had served, so the split could be healed.

teach.h: A HARD SIDE TO THE STORY TOO.
teach.b: His preaching also had a hard side. It came at a time of heavy pressure on Jewish communities in Spain, and historians still weigh his part in it; that belongs in the story too. He died far from home, still on the road.
It closes a week of feet and hands: Frances of Rome, Clement Hofbauer, Nicholas Owen, Turibius, Dismas, Francis of Paola, and now a pair of walking feet.

how: Catholics keep Vincent Ferrer's optional memorial on 5 April; the Dominicans honor him as a preacher of their order, and he is especially remembered in Valencia and in Vannes, in Brittany, where he died.

a Jesuit missionary who sailed to the Americas
a Dominican who preached his way across Europe on foot

games.q: you're Vincent, a respected scholar at the papal court. after a serious illness, you're sent out to preach. what do you do?
o: stay at court and write books.
leave the court and preach on the road.
preach only in your home city.
games.why: he left and walked for the rest of his life, through Spain, France, Italy and beyond, and died far from home.

practice: Think of one place your feet will carry you, the kitchen, the bus, the school pickup line, and ask what the people there would learn about what you love only from watching you, with the sound off.
Choose one small thing that would say it plainly: patience, a kind word, a door held open. If you pray, ask for that; if you don't, simply keep the picture.

wordCard.voice: Vincent Ferrer. A Dominican who left the papal court to walk from town to town, preaching repentance, until he died on the road.

orig.note: Latin: his name as the Church wrote it.

carryVoice: Your line: walking preacher. In the end, the road itself became his pulpit. Until tomorrow.
